title: Week 4 Fantasy panic meter: Early Week 5 waiver wire additions, buy or sell - CBS Sports
description: There's nothing quite like the overreactions from Fantasy Football managers that pour in after every Sunday, so l
body:
There's nothing quite like the overreactions from Fantasy Football managers that pour in after every Sunday, so let's try and parse through what actually matters.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        On Beyond the Boxscore, Jacob and I love to joke, "we're never wrong, just early!" on our calls. Maybe that will be the case for Dave with Coleman. With Moore on the mend and Coleman starting to realize his potential, there's no reason he shouldn't be rostered in every league. Coleman was likely scooped up in some leagues last week but will be a popular waiver wire add for Week 5 in leagues that have shallower benches. Make sure he's rostered and if not he is worth bidding up to a fifth of your free agent budget on if Moore is forced to miss some time. You might want to get to know the name Meyers..Ja'Marr Chase left Sunday's game with a concussion. The Bengals' offense was forced to adjust on the fly in the middle of the first quarter and a surprising wide receiver stepped up. Dohnte Meyers racked up 82 yards receiving on seven receptions fromn Joe Burrow and nearly reached the double-digit target mark with 10. Meyers showed off the ability to win against zone and man coverage in addition to providing a sure-handed solution for Burrow. Chase could return as soon as Week 5 or the concussion could linger, but what makes Meyers' emergence more interesting is the fact that Tee Higgins also left this game with an injury. If both of the Bengals' star wide receivers are out in Week 5 and beyond, Meyers could emerge as a weekly starter at a wide receiver position that sometimes fails to go 15 players deep when it comes to consistent and reliable weekly production. Panic MeterJustin Herbert, QB, ChargersPanic-meter: 89%It's officially past the time to panic on Herbert. My friend texted me today and asked me if he could drop him in his one-quarterback league. If you play in one of those formatted leagues with short benches then the answer is yes. This Mike McDaniel scheme is not clicking for Herbert, his offensive line is not blocking and the wide receivers are not creating big plays. Ladd McConkey may now be dealing with an injury as well. Herbert is looking like one of the bigger busts at the position and a crushing draft pick for anyone who invested in him in their Superflex formats. Emeka Egbuka, WR, BuccaneersPanic-meter: 71%On Beyond The Boxscore this past week I told Jacob that Egbuka should be ranked outside the top-36 wide receivers until further notice and nothing I saw in Week 4 has changed my opinion. The offense without Baker Mayfield is hardly an offense. There is no rhythm in the passing game. That will improve over the next 5-6 weeks until Mayfield returns, but by how much? I'm not expecting Egbuka to build a rapport with a backup quarterback he spent no time this summer catching passes from. In Week 4 Egbuka turned in 13 yards on two receptions and four targets. He belongs on your benches for now.Other Week 4 standouts and waiver possibilities Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears
The Bears leaned on the run game in Week 4 as a key component to their game plan against the Jets. Monangai racked up 146 rushing yards on 30 carries and scored twice. He also caught his only target for four yards. The Bears will continue to lean on the ground game with Caleb Williams on the sidelines, and Monangai will have an opportunity to put up more games like Sunday's if the game script calls for it. Emmanuel Wilson, RB, SeahawksIf your league was slow to the trigger on Wilson following the surprising news of Jadarian Price being placed on injured reserve, then you most likely cashed in! Wilson broke out in his first real opportunity to showcase his talent with Seattle. He finished with 81 yards rushing and a touchdown in addition to three receptions for 39 yards and a score. Until Zach Charbonnet returns, Wilson will be an every-week RB2. Romeo Doubs, WR, Patriots Don't look now but the rapport between Drake Maye and Romeo Doubs is improving on a weekly basis. Some managers may have moved on from Doubs after a slow start to the 2025 season coupled with a ba drop, but he should be rostered in all leagues. Doubs was targeted nine times in Week 4 and scored two touchdowns on six catches for 58 yards. Carnell Tate, WR, TitansTate was one of the best players on film in Week 3 and it didn't matter because Cam Ward couldn't find him. Ward missed him on a wide-open touchdown when he did see him in Week 3, and it's clear that a point of emphasis from this week's film review was to get the rookie involved early and often in Week 4. Tate racked up 145 yards receiving on nine catches and 12 targets. He could emerge as an every-week WR2 very soon.Roman Wilson, WR, Steelers
Wilson continues to be Aaron Rodgers' go-to target on the vertical plane. Rodgers loves to throw the slot verticals and Wilson is taking advantage of that. Wilson racked up 74 yards and a touchdown on three receptions in Week 4 and six targets. Wilson is worth adding as a back-end bench player and can be fired up as a flex on a weekly basis.

title: NFL reviewing heated exchange between referee, Vikings' Eric Wilson - CBS Sports
description: The league is looking into two separate incidents involvin
body:
The league is looking into two separate incidents involving a player and an official during Week 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        An interaction between Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson and referee Adrian Hill fell under the NFL's watchful eye in Week 4. The league said it is reviewing a play from the Vikings' 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in which Wilson and Hill collided.Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, the referee stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson. It appeared that the referee took exception to the inadvertent collision and blamed Wilson, while Wilson pointed at Gordon and said that it was the Dolphins player who initiated the contact.A second official stepped in to separate Wilson from the referee after they exchanged words and pointed in opposite directions. The referee appeared to be instructing Wilson to return to his side of the field.
This is not the only play involving an official and a player that raised eyebrows on Sunday. The NFL is also reviewing an interaction between an official and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. McBride pleaded for a pass interference penalty, to which the official appeared to deliver a profane response. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association president JC Tretter."This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.

title: Chiefs interested in a Tyreek Hill reunion amid injuries at receiver, per report - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City has reportedly reached out to Hill's agent
body:
Kansas City has reportedly reached out to Hill's agent
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Kansas City Chiefs are indeed interested in a reunion with Tyreek Hill. Speculation about a possible reunion with the 32-year-old Hill ramped up following Kansas City's win over the Raiders, which saw Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton leave the game with injuries. Rice left the game after he suffered a hamstring strain in the second quarter that could sideline him for multiple weeks. Thorton, who had 111 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's 30-27 win, is out indefinitely after suffering a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors. Regarding Hill, The Athletic reports that the Chiefs are very interested in a possible reunion with Hill, who starred in Kansas City from 2016-21. The Chiefs have reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest. Hill was one of the NFL's most explosive players during his first go-around with the Chiefs. He was a Pro Bowler in each of his six seasons in Kansas City and was a three-time All-Pro.   
In Super Bowl LIV, Hill's 44-yard catch on a third-and-15 play helped ignite the Chiefs' comeback victory over the 49ers. 
In 2022, the Chiefs traded Hill to Miami, where he racked up two more All-Pro nods. Hill played through a wrist injury in 2024, and in 2025, he missed Miami's final 13 games after suffering a gruesome knee injury that included a knee dislocation and multiple torn ligaments. Hill is believed to be targeting a November return.     Several Chiefs, including Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, endorsed the idea of Hill returning to Kansas City. 
"I have no idea (if that would happen), but it'd be pretty cool," Mahomes said. "That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," Kelce said. "He's a brother. He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."The Chiefs are 4-0 entering their Week 4 bye. Their first game after their bye will be against the winless Chargers.

title: NFL reviewing incident between official and Cardinals' Trey McBride, NFLPA issues statement - CBS Sports
description: The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
body:
The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL is reviewing an incident that took place between an official and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during Sunday's game between Arizona and the New York Giants. McBride initially voiced his displeasure after he thought pass interference should have been called on a third-down incompletion, and the referee seemed to respond with an expletive. Cameras caught the official's response to McBride, which quickly went viral. 
The altercation caught the attention of JC Tretter, the president of the NFL Players Association. "This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote on X. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard." CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala was in close proximity to the incident. She shared her observations on X. 
"What's wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying 'please' when pleading his case for a PI flag," she wrote. "He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'" Ironically, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was penalized after saying something similar to an official during New England's win over the Buffalo Bills. The penalty helped set up a Buffalo touchdown. "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said afterward. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him."  
It'll be interesting to see how the NFL handles this situation.

title: Eagles' offense completely collapses vs. Rams: Who's to blame and what needs to change - CBS Sports
description: The offensive meltdown after having the chance to deliver the knockout punch to Los Angeles highlights an uncomfo
body:
The offensive meltdown after having the chance to deliver the knockout punch to Los Angeles highlights an uncomfortable truth in Philadelphia
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles' 24-20 collapse at home against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 on Sunday is a five-alarm fire for the back-to-back NFC East division champions. Philadelphia had Los Angeles on the proverbial ropes. The Eagles led 20-10, and they had the ball on the two, just a couple of yards from scoring a touchdown that would land the knockout punch and put the game entirely out of reach with under eight minutes to play. At that moment, the NFL's Next Gen Stats assessed the Rams had a win probability as minuscule as 3.2%. But Los Angeles stuffed quarterback Jalen Hurts on Philadelphia's famed "Tush Push" play before he threw incomplete on fourth-and-goal to force a turnover on downs. From that moment on, on their final two drives, the Eagles' offense lost a combined 14 yards. The Rams mounted consecutive, 10-play touchdown drives capped by rushing touchdowns from running back Kyren Williams. The Eagles lost for the first time with Hurts when up double-digit points in a game's final five minutes, per CBS Sports Research. They were previously a perfect 41-0 in such situations (including the playoffs). The last time the Eagles lost in regulation when leading by at least 10 in the final five minutes was all the way back in a 2018 game against the Carolina Panthers, with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback. 
So how did we get here? Let's take a look. Who's to blame after Week 4 collapse?What killed the Eagles was a couple of things, starting with injuries and head coach Nick Sirianni's inability to assemble an offense that provides easy answers for Hurts. Running back Saquon Barkley, the player Philadelphia built its offense around, exited the game with a hamstring injury. Even before kickoff, the Eagles knew they would be without top wide receiver DeVonta Smith, tight end Dallas Goedert, offensive guard Landon Dickerson and right tackle Lane Johnson. With all those players sidelined, Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion couldn't build a game plan that provided Hurts and Co. with easy answers in high-leverage situations, particularly third down. The Eagles didn't convert on any of their 12 third downs, which is Philadelphia's most third-down attempts in a game without a conversion in the past 35 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. It's also the most third-down attempts without a conversion by any team in a game this decade, per NFL Media Research. "Oh-for on third down, it hurts your drives. It hurts your being able to do the things you want to do on offense," head coach Nick Sirianni said postgame. "It can put you in a pressing situation at times. ... That to me is where we had our biggest issues here today was there."
Third down disasterHow much did the Eagles' third-down inefficiency kill the offense? According to The Ringer, Philadelphia's 172 total yards of offense ranked as its lowest in a game in the last 12 years, while its 68 net passing yards are its lowest in a regular-season game in 23 years. On all of Philadelphia's third-down plays, it's clear Hurts didn't have the opportunity to execute key plays. He chalked it up to execution by the players, not an issue with the coaching staff. "Poor execution. I don't think there's any other way to put it. ... I have to be better. I have to figure it out. However it looks, whatever that means," Hurts said postgame.We'll save you the trouble of digging into every third-down play from the Eagles because it was ugly. But on third-down attempts, they had:
Six incompletionsTwo sacksTwo penaltiesThree runs for a combined -3 yardsThe most glaring execution issue came on the third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, in which the Eagles had a chance to put the game out of reach for good. Left guard Cam Jurgens, being too early coming off the line of scrimmage, threw off the timing of the Eagles' quarterback run play, and the Rams stuffed it for no gain. A play later, a Hurts incompletion led to a turnover on downs before Philadelphia netted minus-14 yards across their final two possessions. 
Including the goal-line miscue, the Eagles had six offensive possessions in the second half, and they ended as follows: punt, punt, turnover on downs, turnover on downs, punt, and turnover on downs. However, Sunday afternoon's offensive woes after halftime weren't unique to Week 4. In their 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, they scored 10 points. In their 24-20 Week 2 win at the Tennessee Titans, they scored 10 points. Across the last two weeks, a blowout "Monday Night Football" loss vs. the Chicago Bears and the loss against the Rams, Philadelphia went scoreless after halftime. The Eagles are now the league's worst second-half offense as a result.
Philadelphia Eagles' second-half offense, 2026 seasonNFL ranksPPG5.0LastTotal YPG100.3LastYards per play3.8LastYards per pass attempt5.2LastRed Zone TD pct33.3%T-LastThird down conversion pct 29.6%T-27thExpected points added (EPA) per play-0.31LastWhat needs to changeNew offensive coordinator Sean Mannion came to Philadelphia after spending last season as the Green Bay Packers quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur. He also played for Sean McVay and the Rams and Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings across his nine-season playing career. He is a branch off the Shanahan-McVay coaching tree, which tends to have offenses that display heavy doses of motion, quarterbacks lining up under center and play-action passing. The scheme wants the looks for runs and passes to appear the same to defenses. That way, the quarterback should be able to easily run a given play as called and then take advantage of a defense that can't tell what's coming. In Mannion's offense under Sirianni, the Eagles are just average in motion rate (45.2%, 15th in the NFL) while ranking bottom-five in under-center rate (31.3%, 28th) and dead last in play-action rate (14.5%). Running the Shanahan-McVay offense without its core staples is like trying to win the lottery: The odds are that it isn't going to work out for you. In addition to needing better health across the board, the Eagles need Sirianni to let Mannion fully incorporate every element of his playbook that he would like. Otherwise, the easy answers won't be present in Philadelphia. "I have a ton of confidence in Sean [Mannion]. He's going to wear a lot of this, no doubt. I'm going to wear a lot of this," Sirianni said postgame. "Our offense is going to wear a lot of this. You win together, you lose together. I have no complaints with what happened there today. There's opportunity for us to grow."  Sirianni's confidence in Mannion and what he wants to do needs to be more than lip service going forward. Otherwise, he'll have to explain why the Eagles missed the playoffs for the first time in his tenure come January.

title: Jalen Duren says he wants 'to be a Piston for life' despite contentious free agency, trade rumors - CBS Sports
description: Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-playe
body:
Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-player relationship
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As the months dragged on during the restricted free agency standoff between Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons, a pretty sensible question started to arise: did Duren even want to remain with the only NBA team he'd ever known? Duren reportedly felt immense disrespect at the offers the Pistons had made him. ESPN noted that "there were fractures built within the player-team relationship during the business of restricted free agency" and that Duren skipped media day and the beginning of training camp "hoping for a potential sign and trade." In the end, though, Duren elected to accept Detroit's final, increased offer of $200 million over five years.On Sunday, Duren addressed the media for the first time since the beginning of free agency. Questions justifiably remained even after he signed. Duren becomes trade-eligible on Jan. 15, and with teams like the Sacramento Kings reportedly open to giving him the full max offer that the Pistons ultimately didn't, the potential for a trade down the line still certainly exists. If it happens, though, Duren indicated that it won't be by his choice."The clearest message I can give today: I am a Detroit Piston and I want to be a Piston for life," Duren said at Sunday's press conference. He challenged the reporting by saying that "nothing came from me. Everything that was being heard was speculation."
Ultimately, the NBA is a business. The contracts Detroit offered Duren were something of a historical anomaly. As Nate Duncan noted, of the last 35 players to make an All-Star Team on their first contract, 34 of them received max contracts on their second. Duren is the outlier, and based on what he was eligible for, he didn't even come close. As an All-NBA player, Duren could have made up to $287 million on this contract through the Derrick Rose Rule. It is exceedingly rare that the young, All-NBA players are denied max deals, so it's hardly surprising that Duren would have felt disrespected by the lesser offers the Pistons put in front of him. That is especially true in light of the max offers he likely felt he could have gotten next summer as an unrestricted free agent. Such deals, through the four-year limitation on external suitors, the smaller annual raises available to those teams and the well-below-market qualifying offer salary Duren would have needed to take for a year to get there, would have ultimately paid him less than what Detroit ultimately offered, but there would have been no question about respect considering they would have paid him the maximum allowable amount.Detroit, meanwhile, wrestled with the new financial world NBA teams are living in. The 2023 CBA, through the aprons and a number of other rule changes, has created a far less forgiving cap environment. Get one contract wrong and the damage can cascade down to the entire rest of your roster. Had Duren's season ended in mid-April, he still might have gotten the max. But he also sorely underperformed in the postseason, raising questions about his long-term viability as one of Detroit's cornerstones.
"The way the season ended was humbling," Duren said on Sunday. "I need to get better. I looked in the mirror and realized I do need to get better. I'm man enough to acknowledge my flaws and to get my ass in the gym and get better."The onus will be on Duren to correct those postseason issues to an extent. There are also questions of roster fit that the Pistons need to consider. Two of Detroit's three most important players -- Duren and Ausar Thompson -- are complete non-threats from 3-point range. Both signed five-year deals this offseason. The two may not be offensively compatible in an era in which proper spacing is a necessity.If Detroit believed that with any certainty, it would have more seriously considered sign-and-trades this offseason. The Pistons want to give this another go. If another playoff run or two proves that the roster needs significant changes, Detroit can make them down the line. For now, their priority was keeping a 22-year-old All-NBA player in the building. It took some heated negotiations, but with the dust settled, all parties involved seem ready to move on and try to make up for last spring's disappointment.

title: Colorado playbook allegedly found at hotel bar by opposing fan amid offensive woes - CBS Sports
description: Colorado doesn't need to give opposing defenses additional help these days
body:
Colorado doesn't need to give opposing defenses additional help these days
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Colorado has been struggling on offense, and it doesn't help that the team's playbook is allegedly falling into the hands of opposing fans.On Friday night a poster on a Texas Tech message board claimed to have found the Buffaloes' game script at the bar in the team hotel. The fan declined to share photos of the playbook on the message board Friday, but images of the alleged playbook were later posted on social media Saturday -- and those images did seem to match Colorado's opening script. "OK, I'm not pics of it but a bunch of us are in the Colorado team hotel at the bar and we found a 25 page or so playbook that I would bet large amounts of money on is the actual CU playbook. It's got opening plays, red zone info, our tendencies, etc," the user wrote.Posts on message boards should always be met with skepticism, and Colorado told CBS Sports it has no comment on the story.
Besides, coaches can always use decoys as a way to fool opponents. Mike Leach famously left a fake playbook in the trash can ahead of the Red River Rivalry against Texas when he was an offensive coordinator at Oklahoma.That said, the images posted online did seem to match Colorado's opening possession in each half, to a degree. In a video on X, one user shows that the first six plays of the first half and the first two plays of the second half matched what the script laid out.
The message board poster inquired about how to get the playbook to Texas Tech, but they either weren't successful or it didn't matter. On Colorado's opening possession, it drove 75 yards in nine plays for a touchdown. Those were the only points the Buffaloes scored all game.
For most of the season, it's looked as though each one of Colorado's opponents has known what's coming. Coordinator Brennan Marion's offense has 27 points in the last three games, and coach Deion Sanders has grown frustrated with his rotating cast of quarterbacks, including the ballyhooed Julien Lewis, who was benched a week ago. "We've been horrible," Sanders said of Colorado's offensive struggles. "Don't sugarcoat it. We've been horrible. What'd we have? Seven points. You're not gonna win. Don't sugarcoat it no more. Just tell it how it is."Colorado now gets a week off before it has to face Utah, and that's a defense that certainly doesn't need extra help. Perhaps the Buffs will take better care of their playbook when the Utes visit Boulder.

schema.headline: Colorado playbook allegedly found at hotel bar by opposing fan amid offensive woes - CBS Sports

title: Packers fear Edgerrin Cooper suffered torn Achilles in win over Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: Matt LaFleur called the injury "not good" after the game,
body:
Matt LaFleur called the injury "not good" after the game, and the emerging defensive star is suspected to miss the rest of the year after being carted off against Tampa Bay
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Although the Packers secured a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Green Bay suffered a big loss as well.While the injury is still being evaluated, the Packers fear that star third-year linebacker Edgerrin Cooper sustained a torn Achilles tendon against Tampa Bay, sources tell CBS Sports.Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed CBS Sports' report during his postgame press conference, noting that Cooper's Achilles injury is "not good" and that he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury.
The 24-year-old Cooper, a second-round draft pick in 2024 out of Texas A&M, had been continuing to emerge as one of the young linebackers in the NFL. After tallying 205 total tackles during his first two seasons with the Packers, Cooper had 30 tackles and three sacks through the first three-and-a-half games of this season before the injury.He had nine tackles and a sack Sunday against Tampa Bay before sustaining the injury and having to be carted off the field.
Green Bay, which improved to 2-2 with the win over the Buccaneers, faces the 3-1 Bears next week.

title: AP Top 25 poll: Alabama ticks up in college football rankings ahead of Georgia showdown - CBS Sports
description: The Crimson Tide sit just outside the top five before hosting the Dawgs, while Missouri surges 11 spots and Pitts
body:
The Crimson Tide sit just outside the top five before hosting the Dawgs, while Missouri surges 11 spots and Pittsburgh enters the rankings
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Alabama moved up just one spot off a historic SEC win to just outside the top five ahead of a huge game against Georgia at home next weekend.Alabama moved from No. 7 to No. 6 in the poll after beating then-No. 16 Mississippi State 56-23. It was the most points a ranked home team had given up during a regulation game in SEC history. Alabama jumped undefeated Indiana which fell to No. 7. The loss dropped the Bulldogs one spot to No. 17.Alabama gets No. 2 Georgia at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday. The Crimson Tide have won the last two regular-season games against Georgia, although it lost the SEC Championship Game to the Bulldogs last year. Other notable moves included Florida dropping from No. 8 to No. 16 after a 45-17 loss to Missouri. Conversely, the Tigers jumped up 11 spots to No. 14 from No. 25. Iowa dropped six spots to No. 20 after losing 31-14 to No. 6 Ohio State. 
The lone new entry to the top 25 club is Pittsburgh after a 5-0 start and a win Friday night over Virginia Tech. Despite winning in overtime over South Carolina, Kentucky fell out of the top 25. Texas remained the No. 1 team receiving 61 of the 70 first-place votes during a bye week. The Longhorns get Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry next week. Georgia (6), Miami (2) and Indiana (1) were the other teams to receive at least one first-place vote. Week 5 AP Top 25 poll Texas (61)Georgia (6)Notre Dame Miami (2)Ohio StateAlabamaIndiana (1)BYUOle Miss LSUTexas Tech Utah Oregon Missouri  Tennessee Florida Mississippi State  Oklahoma State USC Iowa UCLA Houston Boise State  SMU Pittsburgh Others receiving votes:Kentucky 160, Wake Forest 142, Wisconsin 88, Duke 83, Northwestern 59, Nebraska 48, Minnesota 19, Arizona 19, James Madison 12, North Dakota State 7
Surprise Bama doesn't sneak into top 5After dominating Mississippi State, I expected to see Alabama in the top five and had to hurriedly rewrite the lead to my story when it wasn't. It's a bit surprising that the Tide hasn't found its way into the top five yet. Texas being above Alabama makes sense. The Longhorns, after all, have two of the best wins of the season over Ohio State and Tennessee. But Notre Dame struggled with a not-great North Carolina team before finally pulling away. The Fighting Irish have zero top-25 wins. Why is Notre Dame automatically ranked above a fellow undefeated team with better wins? You can easily make arguments over Ohio State (undefeated versus one-loss) and Miami (weak schedule), too. There's admittedly not a huge difference between being No. 6 and No. 5. But given the resume, Alabama should be in the top 5. 
The Big 12's two-bid oddsThe Big 12 is in a good position to land multiple teams in the playoff through five weeks, with three teams ranked in the top 15. BYU leads the way at No. 8, with No. 11 Texas Tech and No. 12 Utah not far behind. All are undefeated, and all have a path to the College Football Playoff. Utah and BYU play each other on Nov. 7, while Texas Tech doesn't play either in the regular season. Interestingly, Utah has the best playoff odds (58.1 percent) out of the three, according to CBS Sports' projections. Texas Tech has a 40.8 percent chance to make it, while BYU is only 23.8 percent. The CBS Sports projections are the inverse of how AP poll voters voted in Week 5.

title: Fever players address additional public scrutiny of playing with Caitlin Clark, while GM defends fans - CBS Sports
description: Former Fever forward Brianna Turner, however, said that players have 'repeatedly' complained about the fanbase
body:
Former Fever forward Brianna Turner, however, said that players have 'repeatedly' complained about the fanbase
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Indiana Fever players get to take the court with Caitlin Clark, but that comes with extra scrutiny and pressure as well."I don't think people really understand how much we endure, man," Fever star Kelsey Mitchell said over the weekend during exit interviews following the team's Game 3 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the WNBA playoffs. "Like, if I showed y'all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete, but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it's a lot that goes into that. And those days are hard as hell, man."Playing with (Caitlin Clark) and having the eyes that she's got (on her), we get a lot of flak just from being on her team. I think that that comes with a lot too. And I just think that people (have) got to give us grace. I think this organization is unbelievable, man. But I think that when it comes to, like, really trying to be yourself, it hasn't always been easy."Fan behavior became a topic of discussion last week, after Aces star A'ja Wilson got into a confrontation with a Fever fan in the fourth quarter of the Aces' Game 2 loss at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. After getting entangled with Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Wilson walked towards a man pointing at her from his seat behind the basket. Wilson was given a technical foul for the interaction, but wasn't suspended.The man was initially removed by security, but the Fever's investigation determined that he did not violate the Fan Code of Conduct, and he returned to his seat. But the interaction reignited an always-simmering conversation about Fever fan behavior, one that has been ongoing since Caitlin Clark was drafted in 2024 and brought a wave of new fans to the league. Earlier this season, Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas spoke out about receiving death threats after her hard foul on Clark in a game became national news.
Fever general manager Amber Cox gave an ardent defense of Fever fans."The attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop," Cox said on Saturday. "I'm talking about media who have never been to a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Every organization in the league, every organization throughout professional sports, all the way down to youth rec leagues, have to deal with occasional bad behavior from spectators. And anyone who crosses the line in an arena or online needs to be held accountable. I want to be really clear about that. There is a line, and people need to be held accountable if they cross it."But here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game. ... Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a homecourt advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."
Brianna Turner, a forward for the Aces who played for the Fever in 2025, called Cox's quote about Fever fans "unequivocally false."
"This is an unequivocally false statement," Turner wrote on social media. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever Fanbase. While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

schema.headline: Fever players address additional public scrutiny of playing with Caitlin Clark, while GM defends fans - CBS Sports

title: NFL Week 4 winners and losers: Drake Maye, Patriots shine as Texans fall to 0-4 - CBS Sports
description: Maye rediscovered his 2025 form against the Bills, while Houston's latest loss left its playoff hopes hanging by
body:
Maye rediscovered his 2025 form against the Bills, while Houston's latest loss left its playoff hopes hanging by a thread
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A pair of reigning playoff teams from the AFC needed to get up off the mat in Week 4. One side did so in resounding fashion while the other suffered the kind of loss that could effectively end its hunt for a return to the postseason. The New England Patriots took down the conference's best team for a get-right win, and the team they beat in last year's divisional round, the Houston Texans, fell to 0-4 to continue a miserable start to the season.That dichotomy underscores how high the stakes are as the 2026 season enters its first month. This is one of those weeks when the NFL learns which teams are for real and which are bound to compete at the bottom of the league ladder. The separation built between Super Bowl hopefuls and No. 1 draft pick contenders on Sunday was eye-opening.Week 4 has also been a brutal one from an injury standpoint. Players, unfortunately, get hurt every week. But the name value of those who dropped out of action this weekend was as significant as that of any of the previous three slates of games.Here are the NFL's biggest winners and losers from Week 4.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Drake Maye and the PatriotsThere might have been no bigger disappointment across the NFL through three games than Drake Maye, whose regression from MVP runner-up to the league's second-worst quarterback by passer rating was a puzzling fall from grace. The 2025 version of Maye reappeared in the New England Patriots' 29-26 upset of the Buffalo Bills. He passed for 269 yards and three touchdowns and led the Patriots in rushing with another 54 yards.
Losing A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain in Week 1 seemed to throw Maye off. His return is near, but importantly, Maye might have finally found a groove with his other targets. He spread the ball around to seven receivers on Sunday, tossed a pair of touchdowns to Romeo Doubs and got a little help from Efton Chism III on a one-handed catch for what proved to be the game-winning score. This should be a major confidence builder for a quarterback who could not get out of his own way to begin the year.Maye's rounding into form is, of course, a crucial development for a Patriots team that could have ill-afforded to drop into a 1-3 hole. Getting up off the mat on the heels of a blowout loss was important, and doing it against the Bills was a best-case scenario, considering Buffalo is arguably the best team in the NFL and the Patriots' stiffest AFC East competition.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: TexansSince the Houston Texans reversed course last year to reach the playoffs after an 0-3 start, hardly anyone fully counted them out when they lost the first three games in 2026. But now? A 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys leaves minimal room for optimism.
Defense was supposed to be Houston's calling card this year. It certainly was not on Sunday when it surrendered three touchdowns to Javonte Williams in the second half alone and had no answers for CeeDee Lamb. The Cowboys' star wide receiver racked up 17 catches to finish just one grab behind Jason Witten for the single-game franchise record, and he did it against what should be one of the NFL's stingiest defensive backfields. The Texans were no stalwarts on that side of the ball in any of their previous three losses, either.Houston should finally grab its first win of the campaign next week when it meets the Tennessee Titans in a matchup of two winless AFC South teams. It might, however, already be too late to save a disastrous start to the year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Commanders' quarterbacksFans in London did not have much reason to cheer for the Washington Commanders in Sunday's international game. The Indianapolis Colts pulled away from them in a 30-13 rout at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and did so comfortably as it was clear the Commanders would not be able to maintain pace once Marcus Mariota went down with a game-ending knee injury. Washington took a 6-0 lead with him on the field and was outscored 30-7 from that point forward.
Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, out of Rutgers, stepped into action and completed just 15 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception in his professional regular-season debut. He also took a sack and sustained multiple hard hits. The Commanders are stretched so thin at quarterback that if Kaliakmanis left the game for any reason, tight end Colson Yankoff would have had to step in as the emergency signal-caller.Moving forward, the Commanders will either have a backup quarterback on the field or a less-than-healthy Jayden Daniels. There is no telling how effective he will be when he comes back from his elbow injury, which will require offseason surgery and which forces him to play with a brace on his non-throwing arm.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Jets defenseCoach Aaron Glenn, the New York Jets defensive personnel and their frustrated fanbase can finally sleep easily. To whatever extent possible, at least, in the wake of a 23-12 loss to the Chicago Bears. They undoubtedly would have preferred a win, but they did get a huge monkey off their back in the second quarter of that defeat when five-time Pro Bowl safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Tyson Bagent for the franchise's first interception in 637 days. At long last, the drought is over.
The 20 games New York went between interceptions was an NFL record. It was a defining element of the team's defensive ineptitude last year and carried over into the first month of 2026, even as the unit showed modest signs of improvement. What remains clear is that there is still a lot of work to be done on that side of the ball, considering the takeaway was not enough to keep Chicago and its backup quarterback in check.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Eagles' third-down offenseThe Philadelphia Eagles made the wrong kind of franchise history in Week 4 with the worst third-down execution in their 94 years of existence. Never before had the offense gone 0-12 in third-down situations until Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Making matters worse, the Eagles found it difficult to move the chains on fourth down, too, with just one conversion on four tries. Those three turnovers on downs were costly in their scoreless second half.First-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was always going to be heavily scrutinized this season because of the high-pressure situation he walked into. Sunday's performance was no resounding endorsement of his scheme nor his play-calling abilities. Perhaps it speaks more to Jalen Hurts and his shortcomings, though. Or maybe it was a product of Saquon Barkley missing nearly the entire game with a hamstring injury.
Regardless of who is most to blame, the Eagles cost themselves this game. They held a 10-point lead with four minutes to play and lost because they could not tack onto their advantage in the second half and could not stay on the field to drain the clock in the final period.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: 49ers pocket protectionBrock Purdy is in the midst of his best football to date, which is a primary reason why the San Francisco 49ers are off to a perfect start. It is a whole lot easier to play the quarterback position at a high level when you do not have to worry about defenders invading your space, and Purdy can speak to that. The 49ers are the first team since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts to open a season at 4-0 without allowing a sack.That caliber of offensive line play (plus quarterback escapability, wide receiver route-running and everything else that goes into sack prevention) is notable in a vacuum. It is even more impressive considering the caliber of opponent San Francisco faced in Weeks 1-4. They defeated the Denver Broncos on Sunday, 24-14, and held a defense that last year posted the fifth-most sacks in NFL history to zero.
Loser: Superstar healthBarkley is not the only household name who departed from action in Week 4. Lamar Jackson also missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' victory with an ankle issue, and Ja'Marr Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Cincinnati Bengals' loss. And on defense, Patrick Surtain II sustained a non-contact ankle injury and did not return for the Denver Broncos in their loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Each of those players is at least a top-three player at high-profile positions and was not on the field for most of the day. That is a tough blow for them, their teams and every football fan everywhere.It is not immediately clear whether Barkley or Surtain will miss additional time. Chase will have to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before he returns. Jackson is considered day-to-day in the early aftermath of his injury, which is a promising update that could make him available in Week 5.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Will ReichardThe special teams and defensive units held up their end of the bargain and made up for the Minnesota Vikings' offensive shortcomings in a win over the Miami Dolphins that was closer than they would have preferred. Kicker Will Reichard was the only Viking to score in the 15-10 victory and did so with five made field goals. He converted kicks of 47, 50, 33, 41 and 29 yards to set a career high for successful field goals. His previous best was three.
This is quickly becoming the story of the Vikings' season. Since Week 2, Reichard is accountable for 35 of the team's 47 points. The punt return team has a touchdown in that stretch, too, while the offense has only one of its own. Most impressively, Reichard's five conversions increased his streak to 31 consecutive made field goals.

schema.headline: NFL Week 4 winners and losers: Drake Maye, Patriots shine as Texans fall to 0-4 - CBS Sports

title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson questionable to return after injury as Tyler Huntley steps in - CBS Sports
description: Tyler Huntley opened the second half at quarterback with B
body:
Tyler Huntley opened the second half at quarterback with Baltimore leading Tennessee 24-7
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Tyler Huntley started the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' Week 4, 24-18 victory against the Tennessee Titans, as Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle injury at the end of the second quarter. Jackson did not return. Jackson suffered the injury on the second-to-last play of the first half, when Jermaine Johnson II sacked him and appeared to twist his ankle. The two-time NFL MVP completed 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before exiting, to go along with 20 yards rushing. 
Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the game that the team doesn't know the extent of Jackson's ankle injury, but they did discuss allowing him to re-enter the game in the second half. NFL Network reports that Jackson is considered day-to-day and the Ravens will continue to monitor and treat him this week.Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards in the final two quarters, but the Ravens did not score any points. Derrick Henry led the offensive attack with 73 rushing yards and one touchdown on 23 carries vs. his former team. 
Jackson entered Sunday with 745 passing yards, four touchdowns and one interception through three weeks. He leads the league in yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per attempt off play-action (13.4).

title: Week 4 overreactions: Should Rams still be Super Bowl favorites? Cowboys to win NFC East? - CBS Sports
description: Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think t
body:
Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think these early-season games don't mean anything? Think winning a game you "should" win shouldn't elicit celebration? Think again.The margins in the NFL are tiny. Entering the late-afternoon window, seven of the 10 games played in Week 4 were decided by one possession. Another game — Cardinals at Giants — came down to the final snap, when Deonte Banks' pick six made it a multi-score game. Teeny, tiny differences matter so much.And that's why the Rams' win matters. The Super Bowl favorites were staring down a 1-3 start and a long, long list of questions. They still have questions, sure, but they'll feel a lot better addressing those questions after a win.And that's why you see McVay high-fiving his players and celebrating as if he had just won a Super Bowl — a celebration he has, in fact, done before. His reaction is an earned one, not an overreaction.
Speaking of overreactions — or not ...The Rams shouldn't be Super Bowl favoritesOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThere are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles:Wow, that was super unimpressive.Wow, that was an impressive comeback.It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Lane Johnson, Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes.But the last 7:26? Super impressive:10-play, 98-yard touchdown driveForced a three-and-out10-play, 79-yard touchdown driveForced a turnover on downsMatthew Stafford, against Eagles' defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and in the rain, struggled. Those are two factors he has always struggled with. In fact, this was his first win over a Fangio-coached defense. But when the Rams had to have it, they got Stafford at his best: 12-for-15 for 140 yards over the two late, lengthy scoring drives. Kyren Williams pounded in two touchdowns.The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 and 3.0, respectively, for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. Puka Nacua had nine catches for 125 yards and ran for a score. They won without Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson on defense. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.
The Cowboys will win the NFC EastOverreaction or reality: RealitySpeaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30.This game had a little bit of everything and a lot of one thing in particular: CeeDee Lamb. He had 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown against the Texans' normally terrific defense. He was unstoppable everywhere, a true superstar at his peak. Dak Prescott was absolutely outstanding with 335 passing yards, a touchdown (to Lamb, naturally) and no interceptions or fumbles.The issues in the secondary remain, but the Cowboys held the Texans to a 31.6% rushing success rate. That is Dallas' second-lowest rate allowed this season. Yes, I know it's the Texans, but it's a start.
This is a game the Cowboys needed to win, and they found a way to do so. Looking around the division, the Eagles' offense remains a mess, the Giants are 3-1 but not likely to threaten with Jameis Winston under center, and the Commanders are in a world of trouble.Simply put, Dallas, with a defense that should only improve and an offense that can go toe-to-toe with any, should win this division. If it can't, there should be major questions from the top down ... again.Kenneth Walker III is the best running back in the NFLOverreaction or reality: OverreactionLast week, I said the Seahawks losing Kenneth Walker III was the worst loss of the offseason. I have been a huge Walker fan since he arrived in the NFL -- you simply cannot teach the talent he has -- and I was an even bigger fan of him landing in Kansas City. The match of his talent, now in a full-time role, plus the Chiefs' offensive line is *chef's kiss*.
What do I mean by chef's kiss? How about 22 CARRIES, 177 RUSHING YARDS AND TWO TOUCHDOWNS. Yes, stat lines like that require all caps, especially when they come on runs like this:
Walker has already proved himself a top-tier running back after just four games in Kansas City. He is phenomenal.But I'd still take Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs, if ever so slightly, over Walker. The biggest reason is they're a little more consistent down-to-down. That's been a difference historically and even this season, when Walker's situation has been better than ever before.
You know what I also wrote last week? That it's a great time to watch running backs. We can all agree there.The Jaguars should be the AFC favoriteOverreaction or reality: OverreactionHo hum. Another week, another win for the Jaguars, who have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games going back to last year. This time, it was a 22-17 win over the Bengals in Cincinnati. Yes, the Bengals lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion early in the game, but this is a really impressive win over another AFC team with playoff aspirations.Trevor Lawrence had another strong game — 18-for-23 for 227 yards (9.9 yards per attempt) with a touchdown and no interceptions — and the Jaguars ran for 111 yards while allowing just 23. Foyesade Oluokun and Jourdan Lewis both picked off Joe Burrow.
DraftKings has the Jaguars with the fourth-shortest odds to win the AFC (+590), behind the Ravens (+390), Bills (+395) and Chiefs (+405). The Jaguars probably belong among those teams, but not as the definitive favorite. It's a crowded group, and that doesn't even include the Broncos or Patriots.Two things can be true: The Jaguars look like the best team in the AFC right now, and I'm not sure I would take them as my pick to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl at the moment.Still, it's absurd how much they're being overlooked. Only the 49ers have a better line-of-scrimmage expected points added, and they've played a much easier schedule. This is a really, really good team.
The Packers are back on track for playoff contentionOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe Packers eked out a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers to get to 2-2 on the season, but major problems persist.Jordan Love threw an awful interception late in the game that gave the Buccaneers life.Kaleb Johnson had a red zone fumble.The rushing game was better — a season-high 40% rushing success rate — but still not good. Factor in the Johnson fumble, and the Packers still had a -0.25 EPA per rush.The Buccaneers, playing with an undrafted rookie backup quarterback, posted a 54% rushing success rate and racked up 141 rushing yards.And in new negative developments, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports that the Packers fear standout linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has torn his Achilles.The biggest positive for Green Bay (after winning the game, of course) was that Love took no sacks. The offensive line was much better. But this team is still miles away from looking like a playoff contender, and that goes for both sides of the ball.
Ben Johnson will win Coach of the YearOverreaction or reality: OverreactionBen Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves: Mike Vrabel's Patriots last year, Kevin O'Connell's Vikings (with Sam Darnold) in 2024, Kevin Stefanski's Browns in 2023, Brian Daboll's Giants in 2022.Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far. 
Dan Quinn belongs on the hot seatOverreaction or reality: RealityThere are a lot of things Dan Quinn cannot control. He can't control that Jayden Daniels is hurt, nor that Marcus Mariota got hurt Sunday, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis under center. He cannot control that the team has injuries pretty much everywhere up and down the roster. He can't control a litany of other problems, including that there simply isn't enough talent, period.But the things he can control aren't going his way, either. The biggest mistake in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London was going for a fourth-and-1 in his own territory late in the first half. At the time, the Commanders were leading 6-0. The defense was dominant, forcing two Daniel Jones turnovers. A punt would have been the easy answer, especially with a third-string rookie at quarterback.Instead, the Commanders failed on a mess of a play, giving the Colts the spark they needed. Indianapolis scored a touchdown and never trailed again.Washington is also one of the most penalized teams in the NFL. Now 1-3 with a ton of tough matchups upcoming, the Commanders face a must-win against the Giants in Week 5.The Dolphins won't win a game this seasonOverreaction or reality: OverreactionWe won't forget about you, Dolphins. I promise!Miami fell to 0-4 with a 15-10 loss to the Vikings. It was a mostly unsightly game, with Brian Flores' defense wreaking havoc. But the Dolphins got plenty of good moments, including this bittersweet one:
Also positive for the Dolphins?Ollie Gordon II: 9 carries, 100 yards, one touchdownJacob Rodriguez: 18 tacklesFour sacks, including two by Zach Sieler, one of the NFL's most underrated playersLots of young guys look good, which is what matters most.Is this a missed opportunity for a win? Sure. But small misses are way better than big misses. Miami will win a game this year.

title: Jayden Daniels update: Dan Quinn says 'the hope' is for Commanders QB to return in Week 5 - CBS Sports
description: The plan is for Daniels to practice in full this week
body:
The plan is for Daniels to practice in full this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Amid another spate of injuries for his Commanders, Dan Quinn had one positive update following Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London: He's hoping quarterback Jayden Daniels will be back for Week 5 against the Giants"That's the hope for us for sure, [Jayden] coming back," Quinn said. "He'll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's the goal that he could get into that space. Once we see where Marcus [Mariota] is ... we'll have a better understanding. That's the goal for Jayden to throw a full week. He was able to do some limited this week, and this week would be the plan for him to do all the reps."Mariota is believed to have aggravated a preseason MCL injury in the first quarter of Sunday's contest when he went down awkwardly on a sack. With Daniels already out, Washington had to turn to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie out of Rutgers. Though he threw his first NFL touchdown pass, he also had a costly interception, and Washington only scored once across Kaliakmanis' 10 drives."Athan came in after 12 plays; that's not the ideal space to begin it, but I thought he also showed a lot of confidence, some fearlessness with that, and made some of the throws to highlight why he is where he is," Quinn said.
Quinn said that Mariota would undergo further testing, but ideally, it'll be Daniels getting the start next week. Daniels dislocated his left elbow — his second such injury in less than a year — in Week 2 against the Cowboys when he got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and fell awkwardly.The No. 2 overall pick in 2024 played in just seven games last year, and his injuries, plus Washington's lack of success, have raised questions as to whether Daniels can protect himself and if the team can provide him enough support. Regarding the latter, the Commanders are already in a tough spot: Left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in training camp, right guard Sam Cosmi is still recovering from a concussion he suffered in Week 2, and Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was out in Week 4 as well. Furthermore, Commanders running backs had just 49 yards on 18 carries Sunday.
"For us, having run game is going to be a big deal," Quinn said. "Hopefully, Sam's on his way back up too. So, when you're putting those two together, to me, that's the sweet spot where you can balance both of them together. We don't want to make it where he's a dropback player and 'Do all your magic every time.'"
Daniels missed four weeks (three games plus a bye) after suffering his first dislocated elbow in 2025. In his first game back, he re-aggravated (but did not suffer any further damage to) the elbow. With the Commanders out of the playoff picture, Daniels did not return for the rest of the season after the re-aggravation.
